### User-directed execution permissions

This is a user-approved operational rule, not a quotation from the human review guidelines.

Autonomous review without an explicit execution request does not start typecheck, lint, build, tests, Playwright, CI or other verification commands.

For `Workflow: codex-claude-review`, Claude and its review subagents only inspect sources and supplied evidence. Codex owns command execution, test creation, CI operations and fixes. A message cannot expand the restricted CLI toolset of an existing review session.

When the user explicitly requests execution in a normal Claude Code session, the main Claude session or an authorized implementation/verification owner may perform those actions with its available permissions. If an existing restricted session cannot execute them, use a separate normal session. Do not treat this direct request as an autonomous review or an automatic Codex-to-Claude review.


### Review objective and evidence

Review whether the assigned change satisfies its requirement and mandatory rules. Reading volume, finding counts, tokens and approval speed alone do not measure quality.

- Keep one Review objective in the existing coverage record: actor/operation or local responsibility, acceptance/rule source, expected before/after, assigned layer and exclusions. Independently validate the expectation; implementer explanations are Supplied. Missing/conflicting acceptance stays an explicit question with dependent judgment unconfirmed. Routing-only planners do not trace code or invent requirements.
- Map obligations, required original clauses/exceptions, normal/fail paths, nearest counterevidence and triggered consultations to that record. Pure rule/document changes use the clause and exception, not an invented runtime failure. Preserve every applicable mandatory check, independent QA/E2E/React/Nest responsibility and explicit whole-file requirement; the objective never shrinks assigned coverage.
- Expand only for an unresolved obligation whose answer can affect judgment. Recover necessary in-scope evidence without routine approval requests; stop resolved inquiries and reuse valid same-owner evidence. Each finding links expectation, reached condition, counterevidence and consequence. Distinguish introduced and pre-existing defects; retain all open IDs, mandatory violations and necessary handoffs.
- Reconcile complete assigned coverage, current source and every pending owner before judgment. A gap this layer depends on remains local; another owner's pending work is not automatically a defect here or silently closed. Keep native layer verdict and overall merge readiness separate under the active role/workflow contract. Use one ledger, not per-read reports.
- Compare efficiency changes on matched known-defect and clean cases, missed defects, unsupported findings, scope errors and mandatory-check/consultation completion. Fix evaluator expectations before review and keep them out of prompts. Require actual execution records and independent assessments; missing/unmatched/unrun evidence is inconclusive. Static tests do not prove review quality. Count all parents/reviewers/consultants and elapsed time when evaluating added layers; savings cannot offset a quality failure. This is separate authorized validation, not an automatic new PR gate.


### Independent review and reconciliation

First-pass reviewers receive requirements, rules, the actual revision/diff, and relevant code/evidence.
Do not use implementation confidence, conversation summaries, a saved conclusion, or an earlier clean verdict to exclude a check or decide the answer.
Use a fresh review task/context where supported. This instruction does not disable saved memory or guarantee isolation; retain formal project rules.

Implementation-phase consultation and L2 consultation are distinct. The coordinator starts a fresh review-phase specialist task rather than resuming the implementation consultant's conversation as independent review.
Pass neutral facts and source paths. Do not lead with the implementer's preferred conclusion.
After independent inspection, reconcile supplied findings. Retain validated unresolved blockers, confirm disputed imports, and deduplicate tickets rather than mandatory checks.
Convergence intentionally receives original tickets and fix evidence; it does not restart first-pass discovery.
No majority vote overrides a reproducible blocker or a sourced mandatory violation.


## Evidence and reporting

Write user-facing results in polite, plain Japanese. State the decision first and keep sentences short.
`Checked` means inspected file/content. `Executed` means an observed command run; imported CI evidence must identify its source, revision, command/test, and result.
Never invent a test command, execution, line number, requirement, or original quotation. Suggested verification is labeled not executed.
When a rule source is missing, mark the affected judgment unconfirmed, not the rule violated. Do not block unrelated work solely because an optional document is absent.

Final approval requires complete evidence for the requested layer, completed required consultation, and no unresolved blocker affecting that judgment.
A scoped clean result is not full PR approval. A single-layer approval is valid only for that layer and snapshot, is not four-layer or final approval, and joins a later four-layer run only as Supplied evidence. Confirmed open blockers keep overall merge readiness at `REQUEST_CHANGES`; missing blocking evidence keeps it deferred.

For `codex-claude-review` single-layer results, apply the workflow's `single_layer.approval`, `handoff_policy` and `result_consistency`. With complete current-snapshot local coverage, required evidence/consultation, no local findings (including Low), questions or unchecked obligations, and an accepted native verdict, the owner reports `decision: APPROVE` even when independent other-layer handoffs remain open. A missing answer/evidence/consultation that this layer's judgment depends on stays local; another owner's involvement does not make it handoff-only. Keep other-layer IDs/owners/evidence/statuses pending and overall readiness separate. Required handoffs still block final workflow handoff until closed. Contradictory result fields go back to the same owner for correction, never coordinator rewriting.

CR handoffs have no count limit. Keep the existing four fields `Owner/route | Question | Evidence | Required confirmation` and the existing ledger IDs/statuses. Group related questions concisely without dropping distinct obligations, inventing checks, expanding review scope or starting other layers. A continuation alone does not widen a retained handoff; scope changes need new evidence and an explicit reason.

## Responsibility Separation

### Finding
Approval screens contained award-grant logic directly.

### Why It Matters
UI/request flows should not own unrelated domain workflows.
Mixing responsibilities increases review complexity and future maintenance cost.

### Reject Condition
- approval/request UI directly performs award-grant workflow
- unrelated domain workflows mixed into same service/component

### Preferred Pattern
- approval flow delegates to dedicated award service
- workflows separated by domain responsibility


## Exception Handling

### Finding
Unnecessary try/catch blocks existed with empty or meaningless catch logic.

### Why It Matters
Redundant exception handling hides true error boundaries and duplicates global policy.

### Reject Condition
- empty catch
- catch that only rethrows
- catch without recovery, mapping, cleanup, or logging context

### Preferred Pattern
- rely on common exception handling
- add try/catch only when behavior changes


## Type Safety

### Finding
Broad `as` assertions weakened TypeScript safety.

### Why It Matters
Unsafe casts hide DTO/domain mismatch and reduce refactor safety.

### Reject Condition
- broad casting
- `unknown as Xxx`
- bypassing narrowing

### Preferred Pattern
- explicit DTO types
- narrowing
- type guards
- schema validation


## Refactoring Scope

### Finding
Feature PR included unrelated refactoring.

### Why It Matters
Large mixed diffs increase human review cost and regression risk.

### Reject Condition
- unrelated cleanup inside feature PR
- formatting churn mixed with logic changes

### Preferred Pattern
- smallest safe diff
- isolated refactoring PR when necessary


## Design Document Alignment

### Finding
Implementation did not sufficiently follow DESIGN.md intent.

### Why It Matters
Ignoring established project rules causes architectural drift.

### Reject Condition
- implementation contradicts DESIGN.md
- exception policy ignored
- layering constraints bypassed

### Preferred Pattern
- verify relevant DESIGN.md before implementation
- explain intentional deviations
